svg.title: Downunder Voices Cartoon of the Day — Autopilot has gone fishing
svg.desc: Black-and-white pen-and-ink newspaper cartoon. On the bridge of a new Bass Strait ferry, a relaxed fictional captain with a grey beard and peaked cap sips from a mug marked Skipper and rests one hand on a big old-fashioned wooden ship’s wheel, while a fictional second officer with a ponytail, sleeves rolled up and sweat flying, braces her legs and hauls on the wheel with both hands. The captain says: “Relax, folks — she’s got power steering. It’s called Shaz.” On the console the autopilot unit has a card hanging on it reading Gone Fishing, with a fishing rod poking out of an open window towards the sea. Through the wide bridge windows are rolling swells, seagulls and a lighthouse on a headland. On the wall are a clock, a life ring and a Hand Steering Roster with tally marks. Caption: Autopilot has gone fishing. The crew have gone manual.
svg.text: DOWNUNDER VOICES — CARTOON OF THE DAY
AUTOPILOT HAS GONE FISHING. THE CREW HAVE GONE MANUAL.
Source: ABC News, 22 November 2026 — Regulator orders new Spirit of Tasmania ferries to stay in hand steering for whole voyages.
